purpose: Declarations checked by .agent-harness/scripts/check_ssot_consistency.py. 'facts' are numbers that appear in prose and must agree across every surface: a fact is a value plus the commit it holds at, not a bare number, so a superseded value is legal exactly where it is dated. Every entry is re-verified on every run, so a declaration that no longer describes the repository is an error rather than a silent pass. WHAT IS NO LONGER HERE, and why: 'coverage_policy' listed fourteen claims excused from having to be stated in a live region, because restating a sealed claim by hand produced ceremonial prose rather than checkable prose. D-073 made restating free by GENERATING the board from the registries, so every gate and every claim is stated always and the exemption list has nothing to excuse. 'assertion_exemptions' excused a narrative line whose registry disagreement was corrected later in the same section; prose can no longer assert a status at all, so there is nothing to exempt. Both are removed from DOCUMENT_KEYS as well as from this file -- a key left in the whitelist would be accepted and unread.

facts.description: Result artifacts pinned by digest in .agent-harness/context/LEGACY_RESULTS_MANIFEST.json. The pre-admission boundary is a CLOSED set, so this number must not move without a decision; validate_harness.py reads this value and refuses a manifest whose entries do not match it, and separately refuses one whose canonical entry digest is not LEGACY_MANIFEST_PINNED_SHA256. Growing the set therefore takes coordinated edits to the manifest, this declaration, the pinned digest in the checker, and the prose below -- rather than one commit, which is all it took before (D-070 round-5 review, finding 1).

facts.description: Regression cases in .agent-harness/tests/test_ssot_consistency.py. Round 9's F-R9-007 found the record asserting a suite total that no fact measured, so nothing could catch it drifting; this fact exists so that number is measured rather than remembered. The count is `def test_` lines, so a parametrised case counts once however many inputs it carries -- the B15 bypass family is seven inputs across two definitions. The count RETURNED to 108 at D-073 commit 2, having previously held 108 at `0aa33cf`: nine coverage-floor fixtures were retired when the generated board made their premise unreachable, and five board fixtures were added. The earlier 108 is not carried as a prior because a prior equal to the current value is ambiguous about which commit a reader should trust -- the checker refuses that pair, correctly, and the history is recorded here instead.
